courses.title: Django
courses.description: Django is a high-level, open-source Python web framework designed to help developers build secure, scalable, and maintainable web applications quickly.Its core philosophy is "batteries-included," meaning it comes with almost everything you need out of the box rather than forcing you to integrate third-party libraries for basic features.Key FeaturesBuilt-in Admin Interface: Automatically generates a production-ready administration panel based on your data models.Object-Relational Mapper (ORM): Interact with your database (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL) using Python code instead of writing raw SQL queries.Security Defaults: Provides built-in protection against common web vulnerabilities, including Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and SQL Injection.Authentication System: Includes a pre-built user management system handling sign-ups, logins, password resets, and permissions.Scalability: Handles high-traffic applications seamlessly (used by companies like Instagram, Spotify, and Pinterest).Django Architecture (MVT Pattern)Django follows the Model-View-Template (MVT) architectural pattern:ComponentRoleAnalogous ConceptModelDefines data structures and database relationships.Database LayerViewProcesses user requests, executes business logic, and returns data.Controller LayerTemplateHandles how data is presented to the user (HTML + Django Template Language).Presentation LayerWhen Should You Use Django?Great for: Content-heavy sites, complex web applications, REST APIs (via Django REST Framework), and projects with tight deadlines.Overkill for: Microservices with minimal logic, simple single-page static sites, or lightweight micro-APIs (where Flask or FastAPI might be preferred).
